name: ifcroute
description: Interface and route configuration through socket ioctls, as 2.11BSD's ifconfig and route use them (net/if.c ifioctl, net/route.c rtioctl, through sys_socket.c soo_ioctl).  On lo0, the only interface without a card: a host route added with SIOCADDRT lets a UDP connect to 10.9.9.9 pick 127.0.0.1, and SIOCDELRT takes it away again (ENETUNREACH); SIOCGIFCONF lists lo0's link-level address (4.3BSD-Reno's AF_LINK sockaddr_dl).  Then 2.11BSD's ifconfig(8) on lo0: its status line (2.11BSD's lo0 is UP and LOOPBACK, never RUNNING), `down' and `up' through SIOCSIFFLAGS, and the address and netmask set again through SIOCSIFNETMASK and SIOCSIFADDR; the old FGX ifconfig answered none of these, and upstream's takes exactly one interface.
command: /testbin/ifcprobe -l; ifconfig lo0; ifconfig lo0 down; ifconfig lo0; ifconfig lo0 up; ifconfig lo0 inet 127.0.0.1 netmask 255.0.0.0; ifconfig lo0; D=DO; echo IFC ${D}NE
